card.summary: Holesail is the world's first truly peer-to-peer proxy for TCP and UDP ports. No port forwarding, servers or configuration required.

free_tier.stated: Holesail is the world's first truly peer-to-peer proxy for TCP and UDP ports. No port forwarding, servers or configuration required.

egress.terms: No allowance exists: the bytes travel between the two peers, and the public DHT only coordinates the holepunch.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.interface_detail: npm i holesail -g; holesail --live 3000 prints an hs:// connection string.
record.tooling: npm i holesail -g; holesail --live <port> then holesail <connection-string>.
record.chaining: Carries a WireGuard handshake between a free VM and a laptop without opening a port on either, at the cost of installing a client on both ends.

limits.value: no quota: the vendor documentation lists 'Unlimited bandwidth' with 'No artificial limits or throttling'; throughput is whatever the two peers' paths allow

record.binding_note: Nothing meters the bytes, so at 1 TiB/month the limit is the peer's uplink and NAT behaviour, not a vendor counter.

identity_cost.detail: No account, email or card: the connection string is a public key derived from a keypair generated locally.

record.reliability_note: Depends on public HyperDHT bootstrap nodes; symmetric NAT defeats the holepunch and falls back to TCP, which breaks UDP-only protocols. A harness verified the server side and public-DHT peer discovery on 2026-11-05; the end-to-end data path was not testable in that sandbox.
record.confidence_note: A measured transfer between two peers behind different NATs would show the real throughput and whether the DHT path holds; that is the missing rung.

evidence.proved: Peer-to-peer proxy for TCP and UDP; npm install; connection string replaces a public address.
Launch post: no port forwarding, no VPNs, no servers in the middle, supports both UDP and TCP.
Mechanism: peers announce to HyperDHT, DHT nodes coordinate a UDP holepunch, then UDX carries the data; TCP fallback exists.

evidence.quote: peer discovery on the public DHT works from this network

record.notes: Not a hosted ingress: a third party cannot connect unless they run holesail with the connection string. It qualifies as free UDP capacity between two machines under one control, which covers a WireGuard endpoint only if the far side also runs it. A sandbox verified the server side and public-DHT peer discovery on 2026-11-05 but could not test the data path.

extras.wg_detail: The transport after holepunching is UDX, a custom UDP protocol, with a TCP fallback. A WireGuard datagram can ride that path between two peers running holesail.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance exists: the bytes travel between the two peers, and the public DHT only coordinates the holepunch.
extras.transit_note: Bytes go peer to peer after holepunching; only coordination metadata crosses the public DHT.
